claims.claim: Can be used for storage of any kind of Liquid
claims.evidence: Suitability depends on the chemical compatibility of the plastic and previous contents, which cannot be determined remotely.
The witness report specifically notes that food-grade status was not shown.

claims.claim: Used only once for clean water
claims.evidence: The witness report notes that previous contents were not shown.
The witness observed scuffs and dust; a pressure test or inspection of the base was not reported.
The witness saw bung holes but did not confirm the presence or condition of the actual caps/seals for the stack.

risks.risk: Drums may have previously held toxic chemicals, making them unsafe for water or food.
risks.proof: A clear photo of the manufacturer's embossed markings and any original product labels.
risks.if_unproven: as non-food grade industrial waste containers

risks.risk: The capacity may be lower than standard 200-220 liter drums.
risks.proof: A photo of the capacity marking (L or Gal) embossed on the drum side or top.

risks.risk: Hidden cracks or structural fatigue from UV exposure (brittleness).
risks.proof: A video of a drum being struck or flexed, and a shot of the bottom rim.
risks.if_unproven: as damaged or prone to leaking

proof_requests: Close-up photo of the food-grade symbol (fork and glass icon) or manufacturer markings.
Photo showing the capacity in liters embossed on the plastic.
Photos of the interior of a few drums to check for residue or odors.
Photo of the bung caps/lids removed and laid out to confirm they are complete.
response.reason: The items are identified as plastic drums, allowing for a worst-case valuation as non-food grade industrial containers of unknown capacity.
